matrix.notes: Aggregated first-party NASA data services; each endpoint has its own upstream dataset.
matrix.rate_limit_note: DEMO_KEY works for exploration at 30 requests/hour and 50 requests/day; a free key raises this.

matrix.license_name: U.S. Government work: public domain
matrix.name: NOAA NCEI Climate Data Online API
matrix.notes: Daily and monthly station observations from the U.S. national archive.
matrix.operator: U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, National Centers for Environmental Information
matrix.rate_limit_note: Free token required; 5 requests/second and 10,000 requests/day per token.

matrix.license_name: U.S. Government work: public domain
matrix.name: NIST National Vulnerability Database API
matrix.notes: U.S. national vulnerability repository; each CVE carries an analysis record.
matrix.operator: U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology
matrix.rate_limit_note: Without a key NVD permits 5 requests per 30 seconds; with a key 50 per 30 seconds.

matrix.license_name: U.S. Government work: public domain
matrix.name: National Weather Service API
matrix.notes: The operational forecast API of the U.S. National Weather Service.
matrix.rate_limit_note: No key, but a descriptive User-Agent is mandatory and documented as such.

matrix.license_name: OECD terms and conditions; largely CC BY 4.0
matrix.name: OECD Data Explorer API (SDMX)
matrix.notes: Cross-country comparable indicators produced by an intergovernmental body.
matrix.operator: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
matrix.rate_limit_note: No key required. SDMX REST returns XML or CSV via the format parameter.

matrix.license_name: CC0
matrix.name: OpenAlex API
matrix.notes: A catalogue of works and citations, i.e. a secondary index. The underlying work is what counts as primary evidence.
matrix.rate_limit_note: Polite pool via mailto; 10 requests/second, 100,000 requests/day.

matrix.license_name: Data is openly available; page images may differ
matrix.name: Open Library API
matrix.notes: Bibliographic records only. Presence of a book is not evidence of its contents.
matrix.rate_limit_note: No key; the Internet Archive asks heavier clients to identify themselves.

matrix.license_name: Per-database licences; OSV aggregates upstream advisory databases
matrix.name: OSV (Open Source Vulnerabilities) API
matrix.notes: Aggregates upstream advisory sources (for example the GitHub Advisory Database) and keeps their identifiers.
matrix.operator: Google Open Source Security Team, with the OSV community
matrix.rate_limit_note: No key required for read queries.

matrix.license_name: U.S. Government work: public domain
matrix.name: USPTO Open Data Portal API (PatentsView data)
matrix.notes: Migrated 2026-03-20: the legacy PatentsView website and PatentSearch API (search.patentsview.org/api) moved to the USPTO Open Data Portal, and previously issued PatentsView API keys are not valid for ODP APIs, so this source now takes USPTO_ODP_API_KEY. USPTO states there is no estimated date for reintroducing the PatentsView API functions on ODP; the PatentsView tables are served as ODP bulk datasets, which is what this adapter queries. Reference: https://data.uspto.gov/support/transition-guide/patentsview. The source id is kept as 'patentsview' so records already in the library stay attributable.
matrix.operator: U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (Open Data Portal)
matrix.rate_limit_note: ODP APIs require an API key sent as the X-API-KEY header. Bulk file downloads are capped at 20 per file per year per key (HTTP 429 on the 21st). Documented at https://data.uspto.gov/apis/getting-started and https://data.uspto.gov/apis/bulk-data/download.

matrix.license_name: U.S. Government work; some depositor records carry their own terms
matrix.name: PubChem PUG-REST
matrix.notes: The NIH chemical information repository, with per-record depositor attribution.
matrix.operator: U.S. National Library of Medicine, NCBI
matrix.rate_limit_note: No key required; NCBI asks that clients stay under 5 requests/second.

matrix.license_name: U.S. Government work: generally public domain; some records carry publisher terms
matrix.name: NCBI E-utilities (PubMed)
matrix.notes: Biomedical literature index. The API key is optional but raises the permitted request rate.
matrix.operator: U.S. National Library of Medicine, National Center for Biotechnology Information
matrix.rate_limit_note: 3 requests/second without an API key; 10 requests/second with one.

matrix.license_name: PDB data are available under CC0
matrix.name: RCSB Protein Data Bank Data API
matrix.notes: The single worldwide archive of experimentally determined macromolecular structures.
matrix.operator: RCSB PDB (Rutgers/UCSD/UCSF) for the wwPDB consortium
matrix.rate_limit_note: No key required.

matrix.license_name: U.S. Government work: public domain
matrix.name: SEC EDGAR submissions and full-text search
matrix.notes: The primary filing repository for U.S. public companies. Filings are primary documents.
matrix.rate_limit_note: SEC requires a declared User-Agent with contact details and caps automated access at 10 requests/second.

matrix.license_name: See API terms; some fields carry S2-specific terms
matrix.name: Semantic Scholar Academic Graph API
matrix.notes: Secondary index with abstracts; used for discovery and cross-checking, not as the primary record.
matrix.rate_limit_note: Unauthenticated requests are shared-pool rate limited; a free key raises limits.

matrix.license_name: Post content is CC BY-SA per Stack Exchange terms
matrix.name: Stack Exchange API
matrix.notes: Attention and difficulty signal only. Never used as grounds for a factual claim.
matrix.rate_limit_note: 300 requests/day without a key; a free key raises this to 10,000/day.

matrix.license_name: UN terms of use for statistical data
matrix.name: UN SDG API (United Nations Statistics Division)
matrix.notes: Official SDG indicator series with custodian-agency attributions.
matrix.rate_limit_note: No key required.

matrix.license_name: CC BY 4.0
matrix.name: UniProt REST API
matrix.notes: The reference protein sequence database, curated by hand at reviewed-entry level.
matrix.operator: UniProt Consortium (EMBL-EBI, Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics, PDB)
matrix.rate_limit_note: No key required; the consortium asks that heavy clients throttle.

matrix.license_name: U.S. Government work: public domain
matrix.name: USGS Earthquake Catalog (FDSN event service)
matrix.notes: Authoritative seismic event catalogue with per-event review status.
matrix.rate_limit_note: No key required; USGS asks clients not to send rapid repeated queries.

matrix.license_name: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO for WHO publications; check per indicator
matrix.name: WHO Global Health Observatory OData API
matrix.notes: WHO indicator data, each indicator carrying its own metadata record.
matrix.rate_limit_note: OData reads are open; no key documented.

matrix.license_name: CC BY-SA 4.0 for text; CC0 for some metadata
matrix.name: Wikimedia REST API (Wikipedia)
matrix.notes: Secondary compilation. Used only to orient and to surface citation trails, never as grounds for a factual claim.
matrix.rate_limit_note: No key; a descriptive User-Agent is required by Wikimedia policy.

matrix.license_name: CC BY 4.0
matrix.name: World Bank Indicators API
matrix.notes: Country-level indicators with documented definitions and methodology notes.
matrix.rate_limit_note: No key required; responses paginate at 1000 rows per request.

matrix.license_name: Metadata CC0; each deposit carries its own licence
matrix.name: Zenodo REST API
matrix.notes: CERN-operated repository giving every deposit a DOI.
matrix.rate_limit_note: No key required for public reads; access tokens are only needed to deposit.

features.caveat: The claim states a limit, a negation or an unresolved point.
features.comparison: The claim contains a comparative (more than, faster, ratio, percent).
features.date: The claim contains an ISO date or a four-digit year.
features.evidence: (10 - evidence rank) / 9, the position of the source in the hierarchy.
features.mechanism: The claim contains a causal or enabling phrase (because, enables, requires).
features.quantity: The claim contains a numeric literal.
features.specificity: Word count: 0 below 6 words, 1 between 14 and 45, decaying above.

labels.descriptive: Describes a subject without a quantity of its own.
labels.metadata: A property of a record (licence, language, star count) rather than a finding.
labels.substantive: Carries a quantity, a period or a mechanism and passed verification.

substance_rule.note: The score never changes a verification verdict. It orders claims and labels metadata; it does not accept or reject anything.

epistemic_questions: What do we think we know?

experiments.hypothesis: A threshold pair exists that reproduces every human label in the labelled verification case set with zero false supports.
experiments.method: Exhaustive sweep of 132 threshold combinations, evaluated against 26 hand-labelled claim/document pairs; selection is lexicographic on false supports, recall, F1, macro F1, distance from the documented default, then strictness.

result_json.baseline_name: configured default thresholds support=0.8 partial=0.55 quote_chars=24.0

checks.check: a threshold pair achieves zero false supports on the labelled set
the selected point disagrees with no non-excluded labelled case
the selected point is at least as accurate as the configured default

result_json.conclusion: hypothesis supported by all stated checks

excluded_cases.name: unit substitution not detected
excluded_cases.reason: The verifier compares numeric literals, not unit words, so a currency substitution is not a hard failure. The case is kept in the set so the limitation stays visible, and it is excluded from the threshold selection objective so that it cannot be hidden by tuning.

result_json.falsifier: No swept threshold pair achieves zero false supports, or the best pair disagrees with a non-excluded labelled case.
result_json.hypothesis: A threshold pair exists that reproduces every human label in the labelled verification case set with zero false supports.
result_json.limitation: The labelled cases are synthetic and were written by this project. The measured accuracy therefore reflects agreement with the project's own adjudication standard, and a different annotator could disagree with individual labels. The full case list and the sweep grid are published so that a reviewer can re-label and re-run. The excluded case is published with its reason.
result_json.method: Exhaustive sweep of 132 threshold combinations, evaluated against 26 hand-labelled claim/document pairs; selection is lexicographic on false supports, recall, F1, macro F1, distance from the documented default, then strictness.

experiments.hypothesis: On a shuffled array of 256 distinct integers, merge sort and heapsort use fewer element comparisons than insertion sort; on an already sorted array of the same size, insertion sort uses fewer comparisons than either.
experiments.method: Deterministic in-process benchmark, 15 seeds per input profile, comparison counter per algorithm.
